claims.feature: other: surface polish with nothing underneath
claims.claim: Doctorow argues that prompting a model for a rebuttal yields a blob of plausible sentences that is just stochastic word-salad until a human who understands the issue verifies it line by line.
claims.source: Cory Doctorow, novelist and journalist, Pluralistic, 2 March 2026
claims.quote: you have generated a blob of plausible sentences
claims.page: para. beginning "You haven't generated a rebuttal"

claims.claim: Doctorow describes what a chatbot costlessly produces as infinite volumes of verbose, plausible-seeming topical sentences.
claims.source: Cory Doctorow, novelist and journalist, Pluralistic, 2 March 2026
claims.quote: infinite volumes of verbose, plausible-seeming topical sentences
claims.page: para. beginning "Remember: even the AI companies will tell you"

claims.claim: Mark Williams rejects the premise of AI-spotting, arguing that machine writing does not carry a stable, visible fingerprint.
claims.source: Mark Williams, editor-in-chief, The New Publishing Standard, 16 August 2026
claims.quote: machine writing carries a stable, visible fingerprint

claims.claim: Williams argues that what the supposed AI tells actually mark is the fingerprint of editing - clarity, structure, transitions, a point that goes somewhere - which is a feature of good writing whoever produced the first draft.
claims.source: Mark Williams, editor-in-chief, The New Publishing Standard, 16 August 2026
claims.quote: What it carries is the fingerprint of editing

claims.claim: Williams argues that classifiers cannot reliably separate AI prose from human prose because the models were trained on human prose, so the categories overlap by construction.
claims.source: Mark Williams, editor-in-chief, The New Publishing Standard, 16 August 2026
claims.page: section beginning "So here's the actual argument"

claims.claim: Williams argues that detectors falsely flag non-native English writing because ESL prose tends toward simpler sentence-length variance, safer phrasing and fewer idioms, the very features detectors treat as tells.
claims.source: Mark Williams, editor-in-chief, The New Publishing Standard, 16 August 2026
claims.quote: simpler sentence-length variance, safer phrasing, fewer idioms
claims.page: section beginning "So here's the actual argument"

claims.claim: Williams discloses that the twenty satirical tell-tale signs in his own piece were not written by him but gathered from several AI models, whose sharpest lines he picked and presented as one voice.
claims.source: Mark Williams, editor-in-chief, The New Publishing Standard, 16 August 2026
claims.quote: I put a version of this challenge to several AI models

claims.claim: Strauss reports that the AI-driven author scams she tracks are marked by hyper-personalization coupled with lavish praise, which she attributes to generative AI.
claims.page: para. beginning "The one thing the scammers haven't changed"

claims.claim: Strauss reports that receiving multiple flattering yet suspiciously similar solicitations every day is itself what makes the AI-written approaches start to seem inauthentic.
claims.page: para. beginning "The one thing the scammers haven't changed"

claims.claim: Strauss identifies friendly, open-ended inquiry as a common ingredient of AI marketing solicitations, used to incentivize a reply and draw the writer into a long exchange.
claims.quote: friendly, open-ended inquiry is a common ingredient

claims.claim: In a pre-registered study of 81 participants post-editing LLM drafts for personal writing tasks, the post-edited text still remained stylistically closer to LLM text than to the participants' own unassisted control text.
claims.source: Baumler, Bao, Nghiem, Yang, Carpuat and Daume III, University of Maryland, arXiv:2604.24444, April 2026
claims.quote: post-edited text still remains stylistically closer in style to LLM text

claims.claim: The same study measured post-edited writing as significantly more stylistically homogeneous than unassisted writing, at p = .0002 with Hedges g = 1.42 and a 95% CI of [1.33, 1.51].
claims.source: Baumler et al., University of Maryland, arXiv:2604.24444, April 2026
claims.quote: post-edited writing is indeed more stylistically homogeneous than unassisted writing

claims.feature: other: which features survive human editing
claims.claim: The same study found participants' post-edited text significantly more stylistically similar to other participants' post-edited text than to their own control writing, showing that some features of the LLM stylistic fingerprint are consistently preserved after post-editing across different participants.
claims.source: Baumler et al., University of Maryland, arXiv:2604.24444, April 2026
claims.quote: are consistently preserved after post-editing across different participants

claims.feature: other: which features survive human editing
claims.claim: The study concludes that the human-like changes made during post-editing are meaningfully unique to individuals while the AI-like aspects that are not addressed during post-editing are meaningfully shared between participants.
claims.source: Baumler et al., University of Maryland, arXiv:2604.24444, April 2026
claims.quote: the AI-like aspects that are not addressed during post-editing

claims.claim: In the study's qualitative coding, some participant edits removed words or punctuation commonly associated with LLM-generated text, the examples given being em dashes and the word dive, while others added contractions.
claims.source: Baumler et al., University of Maryland, arXiv:2604.24444, April 2026
claims.quote: some edits removed words or punctuation commonly associated with LLM-generated text

verdicts.trueWording: you have generated a blob of plausible sentences
verdicts.note: Raw page (curl, browser UA). Para. 'You haven't generated a rebuttal: you have generated a blob of plausible sentences ... until a human being who understands the issue goes through the AI output line by line and verifies it, it's just stochastic word-salad.' The prior para. supplies the 'ask an AI to generate a rebuttal for you' limb. Every limb supported.

verdicts.trueWording: generate infinite volumes of verbose, plausible-seeming topical sentences
verdicts.note: Raw page. 'The fact that you can costlessly (to you) generate infinite volumes of verbose, plausible-seeming topical sentences ... time to mark your chatbot's homework.' Costless, infinite-volume and chatbot limbs all present.

verdicts.trueWording: rests on the idea ... It doesn't
verdicts.note: Raw page, section 'Full disclosure'. 'That's not a gotcha aimed at you, the reader. It's aimed at the premise. The whole LinkedIn cottage industry of "spot the bot" rests on the idea that machine writing carries a stable, visible fingerprint. It doesn't.' Byline Mark Williams, Aug 16 2026 (article:published_time 2026-08-16).

verdicts.trueWording: feature of good writing regardless of who or what produced
verdicts.note: Raw page, 'Full disclosure'. 'What it carries is the fingerprint of editing - clarity, structure, transitions, a point that goes somewhere - which is a feature of good writing regardless of who or what produced the first draft.' Claim's 'whoever produced the first draft' is a faithful paraphrase of 'who or what'.

verdicts.trueWording: classifiers can't reliably separate AI prose from human prose
verdicts.note: Raw page, section beginning 'So here's the actual argument.' (line follows it): 'The classifiers can't reliably separate AI prose from human prose because the models were trained on human prose - the categories overlap by construction.' Section pointer correct.

verdicts.trueWording: ESL prose tends toward exactly the features the detectors treat as tells
verdicts.note: Raw page, same section. 'And the false positives aren't randomly distributed. Studies on GPT-detection tools have flagged non-native English writing at dramatically higher rates than native writing, because ESL prose tends toward exactly the features the detectors treat as tells: simpler sentence-length variance, safer phrasing, fewer idioms.' False-positive limb explicit.

verdicts.trueWording: None of those twenty example as written were mine
verdicts.note: Raw page, 'Full disclosure'. 'None of those twenty example as written were mine. True, a few had independently occurred to me, but the truth is I put a version of this challenge to several AI models, gathered their answers, picked the sharpest lines, and presented them here as one voice.' Satirical framing supported by the 'twenty different comedians'/'if you laughed' wording.

verdicts.trueWording: hyper-personalization coupled with lavish praise (thanks to generative AI)
verdicts.note: Raw page (writerbeware.blog, datePublished 2026-08-28, Victoria Strauss). Para. 'The one thing the scammers haven't changed or adapted is the set of markers ...: hyper-personalization coupled with lavish praise (thanks to generative AI) ...'. The generative-AI attribution is the page's own parenthetical.

verdicts.trueWording: multiple flattering yet suspiciously similar solicitations every day
verdicts.note: Raw page, same para. '(when you're getting multiple flattering yet suspiciously similar solicitations every day, they start to seen a tad inauthentic)' [sic 'seen']. Page frames it as the self-undercutting of the scammers' extreme aggressiveness, which is the claim's point.

verdicts.trueWording: intended to incentivize response ... draw the writer in
verdicts.note: Raw page, German-language solicitation section. 'This kind of friendly, open-ended inquiry is a common ingredient of AI marketing solicitations: it's intended to incentivize response, so that the scammer can draw the writer in over an often-lengthy series of email exchanges.' Section pointer correct.

verdicts.trueWording: pre-registered online study (n=81) ... post-edit LLM-generated drafts
verdicts.note: Raw arXiv HTML. Abstract: 'We conduct a pre-registered online study (n=81) in which participants post-edit LLM-generated drafts for writing tasks where personal style matters to them ... However, post-edited text still remains stylistically closer in style to LLM text than to participants' unassisted control text.' All three limbs (pre-registered, 81, personal-style tasks) verified; 81 is the analysed sample of 100 recruited.

Raw arXiv HTML Sec. 6.2 'Post-Editing and Stylistic Homogeneity': 'post-edited writing is indeed more stylistically homogeneous than unassisted writing (H2a, p=.0002, g=1.42, 95% CI: [1.33, 1.51])'. Sec. 5 confirms g is Hedges' g with bootstrap CIs, and significance survives Benjamini-Hochberg.

verdicts.trueWording: significantly more stylistically similar to other participants' post-edited text
verdicts.note: Raw arXiv HTML Sec. 6.2: 'participants' post-edited text is significantly more stylistically similar to other participants' post-edited text than to their own control text (H2c, p=.0002, g=1.14, 95% CI: [1.02, 1.26]) showing that some features of the stylistic fingerprint of LLM-generated text are consistently preserved after post-editing across different participants.'

verdicts.trueWording: human-like changes ... meaningfully unique to individuals
verdicts.note: Raw arXiv HTML Sec. 6.2: 'Between H1a' and H2c, we can see that human-like changes made during post-editing are meaningfully unique to individuals while the AI-like aspects that are not addressed during post-editing are meaningfully shared between participants.' Both limbs verbatim.

verdicts.trueWording: (e.g., em dashes or "dive") or added contractions
verdicts.note: Raw arXiv HTML Sec. 6.4 'What Are(n't) Participants Editing?': 'some edits removed words or punctuation commonly associated with LLM-generated text (e.g., em dashes or "dive") or added contractions, while others reflected more idiosyncratic preferences'. Section pointer and both examples correct.
